statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r is exactly the list of all states obtainable from s by one valid move, each appearing once, in arbitrary order. More precisely, call an index i a valid move index of s when 0 <= i, i+1 < n, and s[i] = s[i+1] = '+'. For a valid move index i, define flip(s,i) to be the byte array v of length n with v[i] = v[i+1] = '-' and v[j] = s[j] for every j with 0 <= j < n and j not in {i,i+1}. Then: (1) for every k with 0 <= k < len(r), there is a unique valid move index i of s such that r[k] = flip(s,i); and (2) for every valid move index i of s, there is a unique k with 0 <= k < len(r) such that r[k] = flip(s,i). In particular, if s has no valid move index then r is the empty list.
preconditions: Let s = currentState and n = len(s). Assume 1 <= n <= 500, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, s[i] is either byte 43 ('+') or byte 45 ('-'). Write '+' for byte 43 and '-' for byte 45.
